outcomes.original: Estimated time: 155 to 365 days. Estimated government cost: $5,370 to $23,350. Notes: This is the timeline and government fee range to obtain approval of the four entitlements (CUA, ABC Type 41, health permit, building permit with change of use) when they are granted, not a time or cost to denial or withdrawal. The critical path is the CUA hearing (120–180 days from filing to Planning Commission decision in April 2022 practice) plus 30 days for the decision to become final, then the ABC investigation and referral review (60–120 days if unprotested; add 30–90 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required for an undue-concentration tract). The building permit and health plan check (21–60 days for DPH review, then 14–120 days for DBI permit issuance depending on plan quality) can overlap with the ABC timeline if construction drawings are ready when the CUA is approved. The health permit to operate (14–45 days after construction is complete) is the last approval before opening. Government fees: CUA application ~$2,700–$3,100 (2022 estimate), ABC Type 41 $1,000–$1,600, DPH plan check $828–$2,207, DPH permit to operate $470, building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction valuation), business registration $55–$700, grease interceptor/FOG $0–$500, sign permit $300–$1,500. State business formation and tax registration (CA SOS $70–$150, seller's permit $0, EDD $0, EIN $0) and employee certifications (food safety manager $100–$250, food handler cards ~$50 for 5 employees, RBS training ~$75 for 5 staff) add roughly $300–$1,000. Private costs not counted here: attorney, architect, expediter, workers' comp insurance premiums, construction, lease, and music licences. The day range assumes a complete CUA application with no requested continuances, an ABC application filed immediately after CUA approval with no protests or PCN delay, complete building plans that pass review on first or second correction cycle, and inspections scheduled promptly.
outcomes.shown: Estimated time: 155 to 365 days. Estimated government cost: $5,370 to $23,350. Notes: This is the timeline and government fee range to obtain approval of the four entitlements (CUA, ABC Type 41, health permit, building permit with change of use) when they are granted, not a time or cost to denial or withdrawal. The critical path is the CUA hearing (120–180 days from filing to Planning Commission decision in April 2022 practice) plus 30 days for the decision to become final, then the ABC investigation and referral review (60–120 days if unprotested; add 30–90 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required for an undue-concentration tract). The building permit and health plan check (21–60 days for DPH review, then 14–120 days for DBI permit issuance depending on plan quality) can overlap with the ABC timeline if construction drawings are ready when the CUA is approved. The health permit to operate (14–45 days after construction is complete) is the last approval before opening. Government fees: CUA application ~$2,700–$3,100 (2022 estimate), ABC Type 41 $1,000–$1,600, DPH plan check $828–$2,207, DPH permit to operate $470, building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction valuation), business registration $55–$700, grease interceptor/FOG $0–$500, sign permit $300–$1,500. State business formation and tax registration (CA SOS $70–$150, seller's permit $0, EDD $0, EIN $0) and employee certifications (food safety manager $100–$250, food handler cards ~$50 for 5 employees, RBS training ~$75 for 5 staff) add roughly $300–$1,000. Private costs not counted here: attorney, architect, expediter, workers' comp insurance premiums, construction, lease, and music licences. The day range assumes a complete CUA application with no requested continuances, an ABC application filed immediately after CUA approval with no protests or PCN delay, complete building plans that pass review on first or second correction cycle, and inspections scheduled promptly.
outcomes.note: The CUA timing references April 2022 practice but the cited records are from 2019-2020. Most government fees (CUA, business registration, sign permit, grease interceptor, state fees, employee certifications) are not in the cited records.
